summary: The root HWN describes something that is low, base, vile, or contemptible. It can also mean something is easy or gentle. In the Quran, it often refers to a state of humiliation or insignificance.
lane: 1 هَانَ ذ , inf. n. هَوَانٌ and هُونٌ (Msb, K) and مَهَانَةٌ , (K,) He, or it, was, or became, low, base, vile, abject, mean, paltry, contemptible, despicable, ignominious, inglorious, and weak; syn. ذَلَّ , (Msb, K,) and حَقُرَ , (Msb,) and ضَعُفَ . (TA.) -b2- هَانَ عَلَيْهِ [ It was of light estimation to him ] It (a thing) was [ easy and ] light to him. (TA.) -b3- هَانَ also, He, or it, was, or became, gentle, and easy. (Msb.)
